title: Beyond the Edge of the Map
story:
James left the gentle murmuring of Tiquiná Creek behind him, his paws padding softly against the damp, red earth of the southern valley path. With every step forward, the jagged peaks of Cloudveil Ridge retreated further into memory, their granite crowns veiled beneath a thick blanket of descending highland mist. The cool morning air smelled richly of damp soil, crushed ferns, and woodsmoke curling from distant cooking fires tucked deep within the hills.

He walked past terraced rows of rustling green maize that rose like quiet sentinels high above his head. He walked past tangled mounds of broad-leafed squash that spilled unruly vines across the drainage ditches. He walked past low stone boundary walls where quick, copper-tailed lizards darted between cushions of wet moss. With each steady stride, the little polished brass compass tapped a reassuring cadence against his chest, its needle remaining true and unwavering.

By early afternoon, the dirt track met another mountain trail at a wide fork known to the highland farmers as the Las Milpas Crossroads. There, rooted beneath an ancient alder tree, sat a flat stone resting bench, hollowed slightly in the center from generations of travelers setting down their heavy tumplines and market packs. James hopped up onto the cool slab, letting the leather strap slip from his shoulder. He drew Barnaby’s brass canister into his lap and gently touched its smooth lid.

It was his fifty-fourth day since taking his very first step out of the Great Canopy, and for the first time, he realized he had walked completely off the parchment. Barnaby’s ink lines ceased at the base of the pass; the wide valley unfolding south existed only in the green sea of earth before him. Sitting on the smooth flagstone as the wind sighed through the cornstalks, James rested his chin on his paws and watched the two trails merge into a single broad lane heading south.
location: The stone resting bench at Las Milpas Crossroads
